description: The one case in this folder where the stored record and the confirmation message DELIBERATELY DISAGREE, and both disagreeing values are asserted side by side. COUSR01C never validates the CONTENT of a user id: :130 tests only 'USERIDI OF COUSR1AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES', so an id carrying an INTERIOR space is non-blank, falls through to WHEN OTHER at :148-150, and is written. This case types the eight-byte value 'AB CD   ' - 'A', 'B', space, 'C', 'D', then three pad spaces - which is not one of the ten seeded keys, so the write succeeds. Two different parts of the program then read that one value and produce two different answers. THE RECORD: :154 is MOVE USERIDI OF COUSR1AI TO SEC-USR-ID, a SAME-WIDTH move - app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:72 declares USERIDI PIC X(8) and app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:18 declares SEC-USR-ID PIC X(08) - so all eight bytes land verbatim, interior space and trailing pad included, and those eight bytes are also the RIDFLD and the KEYLENGTH(8) of the EXEC CICS WRITE at :240-248. KEYS(8,0) restricts the key's WIDTH and says nothing about which byte values it may contain. THE MESSAGE: :256 contributes SEC-USR-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE, which halts the transfer at the FIRST space byte wherever that byte sits - so only 'AB' reaches WS-MESSAGE and 'CD' plus the pad never arrive. Composed literally at :255-258: 'User ' DELIMITED BY SIZE gives all 5 bytes including its trailing space, SEC-USR-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE gives 2, and ' has been added ...' DELIMITED BY SIZE gives all 19, so 5 + 2 + 19 = 26 characters of text: 'User AB has been added ...'. STRING does not pad its receiver, and the MOVE SPACES at :253 is what leaves the tail blank, so WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) holds those 26 characters followed by 54 spaces; :188 then MOVEs it to ERRMSGO PIC X(78), truncating on the RIGHT, giving 26 characters followed by 52 spaces. That is the 26 -> 80 -> 78 chain, and both widths are asserted because they are different observables. THE TWO TRAPS THIS CASE EXISTS TO CATCH. First, DELIMITED BY SPACE is routinely misread as 'strip the trailing padding'. It is not - it is 'stop at the first space'. An implementation written as id.trim(), id.strip(), String.format("User %s has been added ...", id.trim()) or a regex that removes only trailing whitespace yields 29 characters of text instead of 26, which is WRONG; and one that concatenates the padded field with no delimiter at all yields 32. Both are longer than the 26 asserted here, so both fail. Second, an implementation that trims the STORED id writes five bytes where eight are declared, which shortens SEC-USER-DATA below the LENGTH OF SEC-USER-DATA = 80 that :243 sends and breaks the width gate. The six field widths asserted below - 8 + 20 + 20 + 8 + 1 + 23 - sum to exactly 80, and that sum is the self-check that catches a trimmed id and a missing filler alike. SEC-USR-FILLER is a NAMED span, not an anonymous gap; COUSR01C assigns it nowhere and it must still be emitted as 23 spaces, which app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl corroborates by pushing the 57-character rows through IEBGENER into a DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) dataset at :48 before STEP02 defines RECORDSIZE(80,80) at :66 and STEP03 REPROs into it. WHY THE MESSAGE CAN STILL READ THE ID. The DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm runs in source order: :252 PERFORM INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS first, then :253 MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE, then :254 MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC, then the STRING at :255-258, then :259 PERFORM SEND-USRADD-SCREEN. INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :287-295 blanks USERIDI, FNAMEI, LNAMEI, PASSWDI, USRTYPEI and WS-MESSAGE but NOT SEC-USR-ID, which is precisely why the STRING two lines later still has an id to read. That ordering is observable twice over: the five data items go out blank at 20/20/8/8/1 while the record keeps 'AB CD   ', and the cursor is on FNAMEL from :289. ROW INDEX, AND WHICH INTERPRETATION WAS USED. ParityCase documents two different meanings for rowIndex and this case relies on both, one per member. In expectedWrites rowIndex is the 0-based WRITE ORDINAL, and there is exactly one write, so it is 0. In expectedFinalState rowIndex is the 0-based DATASET ROW POSITION after the run, and USRSEC is a key-sequenced cluster - app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:64-73 defines it KEYS(8,0) RECORDSIZE(80,80) INDEXED - so position is key sequence. Comparing 'AB CD   ' with the smallest seeded key 'ADMIN001' byte by byte in US-ASCII: position 1 'A' equals 'A'; position 2 'B' is x'42' against 'D' at x'44', so 'B' is less. 'AB CD   ' therefore sorts ahead of every seeded key and lands at final-state position 0, shifting ADMIN001 through USER0005 to positions 1 through 10. The two readings happen to give the same number here, and that coincidence is stated rather than left to hide the question. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM THE FOLDER'S OTHER SUCCESSFUL WRITES. case01 stores 'NEWUSR01' and case11 stores 'newusr01' - eight full characters with no space at all, so DELIMITED BY SPACE transfers the whole field and the record and the message agree. case12 stores 'AB      ' - two characters and six TRAILING pad spaces - so the two also agree there, and crucially a trim-based implementation would still pass it. Only an INTERIOR space separates the two readings, which is what this case supplies and why it is the folder's strongest byte-exactness proof. WHAT IS NOT HERE. COPY DFHATTR at COUSR01C.cbl:57 is COMMENTED OUT, so no DFHATTR constant is compiled in and none is asserted; DFHGREEN is a DFHBMSCA value reproduced in common.BmsAttributes from IBM CICS documentation, because DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are all absent from this repository. COUSR01C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY - verified zero occurrences - so there is no '*' marker and no per-field DFHRED anywhere on this path; MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :254 is the single attribute assignment in the whole program. The payload also arrives carrying deliberate rubbish in all six header items and in ERRMSGI: RECEIVE at :89 genuinely overlays the whole map, and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :214-233 then overwrites all six while :188 overwrites ERRMSGO, so what goes out is 'CU01', the two COTTL01Y titles from :19 and :22, 'COUSR01C', and the pinned clock as 07/19/22 and 23:12:34 - never the received rubbish. The sixteen CARDDEMO-COMMAREA images travel through byte for byte and total COCOM01Y's 160, because this program writes only CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT and the three RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN fields and the two lines at :172-173 that would have set the user fields are commented out. State lives in the payload and in no session. SEC-USR-PWD is the plaintext 'PASSWORD' exactly as CSUSR01Y declares it and COSGN00C compares it; hashing it would change behaviour and is out of scope. PROVENANCE. These expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED and were NEVER captured from a running COBOL program - executing the legacy programs is impossible in this environment, with eight independently verified blockers including a compiler reporting 'indexed file handler : disabled', no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator and the three IBM copybooks absent. They come from structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:130 (the blank-only guard that lets an interior space through), :148-160 (the fall-through and the five same-width stores), :238-259 (the write and its NORMAL arm) and especially the STRING at :255-258, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:18-23 for the six-field 80-byte layout, app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:72 for USERIDI PIC X(8) and :90/:164 for the 78-byte ERRMSGI/ERRMSGO pair, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-89 and :93 for the FILE(USRSEC) ... ADD(YES) binding, app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten 57-character seed rows and :64-73 for the cluster definition, and app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:19 and :22 for the title literals. One step is not an inference from this source at all: that DELIMITED BY SPACE halts at the FIRST space rather than stripping a trailing pad is a COBOL STRING language rule, and it is applied as such. The record images are stated at the copybook's 80 bytes while the seed rows are stated at the JCL's 57, because FieldDiffer owns the USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 pad and applies it at seed time - so a width disagreement in a failure is always a real difference. Both message channels are declared because WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) and ERRMSGO PIC X(78) are different observables and the two bytes :188 drops are exactly what distinguishes them; the 78-byte line is the one a terminal sees. The code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII and the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the instant this source's own version footer carries, so nothing here reads a platform default or a wall clock.
